# HAZARD ZONES The Commanding Officer divides the colony into four zones, each with its own protective posture. Changes are posted on the front page and may come at any shift change. If a sign and a sentry disagree, the sentry is right.
## ZONE GREEN - MOPP 0 [color=#9FC46A][bold]OPEN[/bold][/color] - Living blocks, the mess, shops, the clinic waiting room and the bar. - No checks. Patrols pass through. Carry your ID and know where your mask is.
## ZONE AMBER - MOPP 1 [color=#F2D21B][bold]CONTROLLED[/bold][/color] - Landing pads, fuel stores, the power plant, the atmosphere and water works, the comms relay and Colony Administration. - ID checked at the door. Bags may be searched. Masks carried, not worn. No loitering, no photographs.
## ZONE RED - MOPP 2 [color=#F28C1B][bold]RESTRICTED[/bold][/color] - The garrison compound, armoury, decon station, vehicle park, command post and the perimeter fence line. - Entry only under escort with a written pass. Sentries are authorised to use force to stop an intruder.
## ZONE BLACK - MOPP 4 [color=#FFFFFF][bold]EXCLUSION[/bold][/color] - Declared during an emergency: a gas leak, a fire, a cave-in, a quarantine, a spill, unexploded charges or a firefight. - Nobody crosses the cordon without full protection and an assignment to the response. When the air is bad, the line is the line.
## MARKINGS - Chevron striping on a barrier marks the edge of a zone. - Hazard striping marks a checkpoint or decon lane. Stop at the painted bar. - Flashing amber lights on a cordon mean Zone Black. Turn around and hold your breath.
Zone changes are also carried by the [netlink="Colony Herald" link="herald.colony.news"] when the press is on shift.
